note: Adapted from the original English description of Scheffrahn & Křeček 1999, where the species was established as Cryptotermes cylindroceps n. sp.; type locality Santa Barbara, Curaçao; known from the three islands of Aruba, Curaçao and Bonaire, and the most common drywood termite in that range (the authors state that their specimens account for more than half of the drywood termites collected there). Alates: 5 females and 13 males from 9 colonies; soldiers: 18 individuals from 12 colonies. The specific name refers to the cylindrical soldier head capsule; the authors note that its colour resembles C. brevis but is darker, that it has an arolium, and that all its measurements are smaller than those of C. brevis.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body brown to yellowish brown, rather variable. Frontal face pale brown, the vertex brown or yellowish brown; a darker narrow band between the compound eyes and the occiput. Chevron on the forewing scale distinct and brown, or paler and yellowish brown. Sclerotized forewing veins brown or yellowish brown, the wing membrane nearly transparent. Antennae, pronotum and abdominal tergites brown to yellowish brown. Labrum pale brown. Femora yellowish white, the ends of the legs (including the tibiae) slightly darker, pale yellowish brown. Abdominal sternites pale brown or yellowish brown. Head nearly oval, the cranial sutures distinct. Compound eyes medium-sized, not protruding, nearly circular. Ocelli large, oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 14—17-segmented, usually 15 or 16; the usual segment formula 2=3=4=5, less often 2<3=4=5 or 2<3>4=5. Anterior margin of the pronotum concave, the sides slightly convex, the posterior margin shallowly concave. Pronotum usually with a distinct median line and a weak transverse band spot. Radius of the forewing meeting the wing margin at one fifth or one quarter of the wing length from the suture; radial sector with 7—9 branches. Arolium present.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Measurements (5 females and 13 males, 9 colonies, in mm, the morphotype in parentheses): head length including the labrum 1.10—1.26 (1.19±0.035, 1.19); head length to the postclypeus 0.77—0.87 (0.82±0.021, 0.83); maximum head width across the compound eyes 0.93—1.00 (0.96±0.021, 0.96); compound eye diameter 0.27—0.30 (0.29±0.0096, 0.30); shortest distance from the compound eye to the posterior margin of the head 0.15—0.18 (0.16±0.0097, 0.15); ocellus diameter 0.13—0.16 (0.14±0.0075, 0.15); maximum pronotal length 0.61—0.69 (0.65±0.023, 0.67); maximum pronotal width 0.75—0.92 (0.85±0.040, 0.83); total body length with wings 8.02—8.80 (8.41±0.22, 8.66); total body length without wings 3.69—4.97 (4.30±0.38, 3.83); forewing length (from the suture) 6.53—7.10 (6.75±0.15, 6.96); maximum forewing width 1.75—2.04 (1.87±0.080, 1.86).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, in dorsal view, almost black from the anterior fifth to half, grading posteriorly to chestnut brown or dark chestnut brown, the posterior fifth orange-yellow; in lateral view almost black on the anterior fifth, chestnut brown behind, with an orange-yellow band along the foramen magnum. Mandibles very dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty orange, the remainder pale yellow. Head, in dorsal view, nearly square, the sides nearly parallel; the anterior margin slightly concave, the posterior margin slightly convex; some specimens with a shallow constriction on the anterior third and the posterior part slightly bulbous, others with the sides slightly divergent anteriorly. Head rugae reticulate, fine and shallow, more distinct near the frontal margin, fading posteriorly, and extending to the genal horns and the genae. Frontal margin distinct from the frontal face but continuous with the vertex; its outline nearly circular in frontal view. Frontal face shallowly concave, with a flat shining area in the middle, densely rugose around the margin; frontal face meeting the vertex face at 70—90°. Labrum short, ligulate, swollen at the apex, the apical margin with rather short hairs. Frontal horns rounded, broad and short, almost continuous with the frontal margin, directed forward, with a deep depression between them and the clypeus. Genal horns distinct, twice as long as wide, cylindrical, conical at the tip, often with a shallow constriction at the base, the surface granular; in lateral view the genal horns close to the base of the frontal horns, and in dorsal view the frontal horns do not conceal the genal horns. Mandibles extremely short, in some specimens slightly raised at the base, bent about 65°; the apical teeth of both mandibles reduced and oblique; slightly curved downwards in lateral view. When closed, the tip of the right mandible is concealed by the tip of the left mandible.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements (18 individuals, 12 colonies, in mm, holotype): head length to the tip of the mandibles 1.40—1.60 (1.52±0.046, 1.48); head length to the frontal horns 1.18—1.32 (1.27±0.037, 1.22); frontal margin width 1.02—1.18 (1.10±0.047, 1.06); outer span of the frontal horns 0.77—0.88 (0.84±0.027, 0.85); maximum head width 1.06—1.23 (1.15±0.051, 1.11); head height without the postmentum 0.90—1.06 (0.98±0.050, 1.00); maximum pronotal width 1.05—1.23 (1.11±0.051, 1.09); maximum pronotal length 0.72—0.87 (0.78±0.043, 0.74); left mandible length (apex to ventral articulation) 0.51—0.60 (0.55±0.025, 0.56); total body length 3.07—4.90 (3.70±0.44, 3.22).
